Organization repositories (`subculture-collective`) use GitHub as `origin`: push the branch there and open the PR with `gh pr create`. A ready PR merges itself once its required check (`CI gate` or `Mirror CI gate`) passes and it has no conflicts; to hold it, open it as a draft or add the label `hold`. Never push an organization repository to its Gitea copy: Gitea is a fast-forward mirror, and the `gitea` remote is fetch-only. A fresh GitHub clone has no `gitea` remote, so commit with command-local `-c user.name='SUBCULT Agent' -c user.email='info@subcult.tv'`.

## Where issues live

Since 2026-11-10 every `subculture-collective` organization repository takes branches and PRs on GitHub, and Gitea holds a fast-forward mirror. Issues depend on visibility:

- **Public organization repositories**: new issues go on GitHub, where Issues, Projects and (on products) Discussions are on. Older issues may still be on Gitea until they are moved.
- **Private organization repositories and repositories that exist only on Gitea**: issues stay on Gitea.

`scripts/roadmap.py` publishes to Gitea only. Use it where issues live on Gitea. For a public organization repository, do not publish to the Gitea copy: check the plan with the script as usual, then create the issues on GitHub with `gh issue create` in the printed order, using the `--preview` bodies, and record order with `Blocked by #n` lines. In a GitHub PR, `Closes #n` refers to GitHub's own issue numbers; link a work issue still on Gitea by its full URL.

Find the tracker. Public `subculture-collective` organization repositories take new issues on GitHub: use `gh issue create`. Private organization repositories and repositories that exist only on Gitea keep issues on Gitea (`git.subcult.tv`): use `tea issues create --login subcult-agent --repo <owner>/<repo> --title ... --description-file -`, with the owner and name from the `gitea` remote when `origin` is GitHub. Other GitHub repositories use `gh issue create`.
Check `git remote -v` to find the tracker. For Gitea or Forgejo, use `tea issues create --login <login> --repo <owner>/<repo> --title ... --description-file -`. For GitHub, use `gh issue create`.
